_comment: First real (non-dry) retraining run -- WBS 4.3.5, 2026-08-17, Colab T4.
The pipeline had only ever been exercised with --dry-run, which stops after
the snapshot. This run executed the whole path: snapshot -> fine-tune ->
score both checkpoints on the same rows -> promotion gate. `skipped_reason`
is null, meaning the gate actually ran rather than being unable to find a
Committed here rather than beside the checkpoint because ai/models/*/ is
git-ignored. The candidate weights (~1.1 GB) live only in Google Drive at
MyDrive/bantai/retraining_runs/ -- they are regenerable from this manifest:
same labeled dataset, same seed 42, same training code.

baseline_checkpoint._comment: Verified in-notebook against the deployed ai/models/xlm-roberta-smishing/ before scoring, so the gate is known to have compared against the model actually in service.

decision.reason: significantly better: 97 fixes vs 44 regressions (p=0.0000), macro-F1 0.9520 -> 0.9648

zero_reports_was_deliberate: No validated user reports existed. The only ones ever created were a
smoke-test fixture with invented message bodies, deleted before this run:
training a real checkpoint on fabricated SMS would contaminate every
figure derived from it. The manifest records `null (no report store
consulted)` rather than a zero that could be misread as 'none were filed'.
the_comparison_is_conservative: AI_MODEL_RESULTS.md records the deployed model at macro-F1 0.9438 on its
own 2,785-row validation split. Here the same checkpoint scored 0.9520.
That ~0.8pp gap is the bias retraining/pipeline.py's docstring predicted,
now observed rather than theorised. The dataset grew after 2026-07-29, so
the stratified 80/20 split partitions differently, and some rows the
baseline trained on now sit in the validation set -- it was partly graded
The bias therefore favours the INCUMBENT. The candidate cleared a bar that
is, if anything, slightly too high, so the true gap is likely wider than
what_drove_the_improvement: DEV_LOG 2026-07-30 records 1,050 + 447 genuinely-new messages folded into
the dataset -- the day after the baseline was trained. The candidate
learned from roughly 1,000 rows (post-deduplication) the incumbent has
never seen. No relabelling occurred in that window (the Kaggle/NTC
mislabelling fix predates the baseline, 2026-07-22), so the gain is not a
why_nothing_was_promoted: Promotion is a separate, deliberate decision and this one is expensive.
Campaign centroids live in the embedding space of the checkpoint that
produced them, so a swap requires re-running embed_dataset.py and
cluster_campaigns.py. Worse, PIPELINE.md's Stage 5b warning applies
directly: the Sprint 5 threshold work -- the 0.85 -> 0.999 recalibration,
the three-tier hybrid lexical gates, the embedding-centering bracket -- was
all measured against the 2026-07-29 checkpoint. Promoting invalidates every
one of those numbers and requires re-calibrating from scratch.
Those numbers are currently with the adviser awaiting sign-off. Swapping
the model underneath a review in progress is the worst available timing.
Recorded as a fifth item for that sign-off instead.
known_gap: 44 regressions are counted but not identified. The gate records how many
messages the candidate got wrong that the baseline got right, not which
ones. A panel asking 'what got worse?' cannot be answered from this file.
Fixable by having evaluate_candidate persist the disagreeing indices.
